verdict.rationale: Cognee's first-party docs and pricing page say it is open source and that the full memory engine can run locally or on your own stack. The docs also give a single-command Docker quick start (cognee/cognee:main) for custom deployments, and the UI and pipelines can run entirely on your own machine with no account. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of self-hosted deployments, production-grade self-host guidance (e.g. docker-compose/Kubernetes, backing-store configuration) beyond the dev-oriented single-container quick start.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can self-host the memory layer from open-source code (e.g. via Docker) on infrastructure I control

citations.quote: Cognee is open source. Run the full memory engine locally or on your own stack — free, forever.
Run Cognee locally using Docker for development, testing, and custom deployments.
Quick start with Docker (single command): docker run --env-file ./.env -p 8000:8000 --rm -it cognee/cognee:main
you can also run the UI and all pipelines entirely on your own machine for free, with no account required, using `cognee.start_ui()`.
